paper.title: ChemAgent: Self-updating Library in Large Language Models Improves Chemical Reasoning
paper.central_claim: ChemAgent decomposes chemistry problems into atomic sub-tasks and uses a self-updating library (planning, execution and knowledge memory) plus evaluation & refinement, improving LLM chemical reasoning on four SciBench chemistry sets (up to 46% over direct reasoning, ~10% over StructChem with GPT-4) and improving with experience.
paper.scope_class: A: runtime-extended planning/execution memory; B: development-set library construction

assessment.evidence_level_note: The full pipeline improves test accuracy, but the retained library's own contribution is not shown: Mp+Me alone equals no memory, the memory on/off contrast includes the non-retained Mk, and the self-evolution curve uses test-answer correctness on repeated test passes (EVIDENCE rule 2). Shared seat value 'retained' corrected.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported, single run: with GPT-4-1106, the full ChemAgent pipeline (decomposition, per-problem LLM knowledge generation, dev-built library retrieval, evaluation & refinement) averages 57.2 vs 47.7 for literature-reported StructChem on SciBench chemistry test sets (gain concentrated on CHEMMC/MATTER); the retained library's contribution is not established and the 46% figure is an absolute-point gap on one 39-item set.
unresolved: Retained-library effect not isolated (no Mk-only arm; Mp+Me alone = none).
ATKINS 61.18 vs n=107 and abstract/conclusion 46%/36% inconsistencies unexplained.

G.reason: Error types of chemical reasoning are illustrated and StructChem is the nearest chemistry baseline, but 'lack of memory' is not diagnosed as the binding bottleneck (the paper's own error analysis puts question understanding first) and external-memory/workflow-reuse neighbours are dismissed in one sentence without comparison.

M.reason: Atomic (condition, sub-task, solution) units with similarity retrieval plausibly address formula/constant/unit errors and give testable predictions (memory quality matters). Key mechanism assumptions are thin on their own terms: knowledge memory and the synthetic-execution-memory fallback are generated from the same model's parametric knowledge (no new information to correct its errors), and four interacting modules are stacked without an argued per-module role. (Results-based weaknesses are judged in E, not here.)

X.reason: Algorithm 1, prompts and retrieval caps (2/4-shot) reconstructible; similarity/confidence threshold values missing; runtime write gate described inconsistently (§2.5 no check vs §2.9 correct-only); no forgetting/conflict/versioning; hybrid memory degrades without remedy.

E.measurement.reason: Endpoint metric is numeric agreement with ground truth at 1% relative tolerance, a credible verifier for these textbook problems. Not 4: a published decomposition example carries a unit error the pipeline certified, and baseline rows come from other papers (fairness judged under E.causality).

E.causality.reason: Ablations exist but the claimed causal source is not supported: the retained library alone (Mp+Me, no Mk) equals no memory (51.53 = 51.53); fixed human few-shot examples in place of execution memory tie the full memory (53.71); memory on/off is +5/229 problems in a single run and includes the non-retained Mk; the large gains over baselines come from the whole pipeline with copied literature baselines and a possibly stronger E&R model. Evidence partly contradicts attribution to the self-updating library.

E.holdout.reason: Initial library built from a separate 43-item development set and evaluated on 229 test items (clean); but runtime updates write from the test stream, and the self-evolution experiment admits memories by test-answer correctness over repeated passes on the same 49 MATTER items with only own-problem exclusion (A2 oracle signal); no contamination analysis; chemistry only.

E.statistics.reason: Main GPT-4 results (Table 1) are single runs with no intervals; differences are 1–6 problems per dataset; ATKINS 61.18% is unattainable with n=107 and Tables 1/2 average the same rows differently, so headline denominators are not internally consistent. Repeats exist only for open models (means, no SD) and the MATTER evolution/shot curves; auxiliary chi-square/Mann-Whitney tests concern retrieval similarity, not the main gains (A2 ladder 1: main results without uncertainty).
search_scope: Tables 1–6, Fig. 5/9 captions, App. B–D: main-result CI/seed/variance absent
